uncited: This family encompasses methods that treat volume rendering as a differentiable operation to solve inverse problems, optimizing 3D scene representations from 2D observations without requiring 3D ground truth supervision [Differentiable volume rendering](43-differentiable-volume-rendering.md).

It sets itself apart from [Radiance-field optimization](44-radiance-field-optimization.md) by focusing on the general differentiability of the volume rendering integral rather than specific neural field architectures, and from [Tomographic reconstruction as inverse rendering](45-tomographic-reconstruction-as-inverse-rendering.md) by encompassing both tomographic and non-tomographic (e.g., RGB-only) optimization loops [Differentiable volume rendering](43-differentiable-volume-rendering.md).

All methods in this family rely on the differentiability of the forward rendering operator and the propagation of gradients through the integration steps [Radiance-field optimization](44-radiance-field-optimization.md).

The core mechanism is the evaluation of the volume rendering equation and the computation of gradients with respect to scene parameters (density, geometry, transfer functions, camera poses) [Radiance-field optimization](44-radiance-field-optimization.md).

where $\sigma_i$ is the density, $\delta_i$ is the step size, $\mathbf{c}_i$ is the color, and $T_i = \exp\left(-\sum_{j=1}^{i-1} \sigma_j \delta_j\right)$ is the transmittance [Radiance-field optimization](44-radiance-field-optimization.md).
**Reverse-Mode Automatic Differentiation (AD):** Standard backpropagation through the computational graph.
This requires storing $O(kn)$ intermediate states (where $n$ is pixels and $k$ is samples), leading to high memory usage [Radiance-field optimization](44-radiance-field-optimization.md).
**Adjoint Method:** Computes gradients by propagating adjoint variables backward through the rendering algorithm, evaluating the chain rule from output to input.

This has computational complexity largely constant in the number of parameters, making it preferable for optimizing many parameters like the transfer function [Radiance-field optimization](44-radiance-field-optimization.md).

**Analytic Inversion / Explicit Gradients:** Uses a-priori knowledge of the DVR operations to invert the order of operations or derive closed-form gradients, reducing memory consumption to $O(n)$ by avoiding the storage of intermediate results [Radiance-field optimization](44-radiance-field-optimization.md).

The integration of differentiability into volume rendering emerged from the need to optimize 3D structures from 2D data without explicit 3D supervision [Differentiable volume rendering](43-differentiable-volume-rendering.md).

Early work focused on analytic gradients for differentiable volume rendering [Differentiable volume rendering](43-differentiable-volume-rendering.md), while later developments unified tomographic reconstruction with inverse rendering techniques [Tomographic reconstruction as inverse rendering](45-tomographic-reconstruction-as-inverse-rendering.md).
